messages:
Alex: Heads up — saw a 3x tail latency spike in eu-west3 around 02:00 UTC. Correlates with a batch of quantized finetune jobs + large checkpoint uploads. Egress bytes + KV-cache churn both flash high. Anyone else seeing this?
Priya: saw the same. kube-events noise + NIC tx queue saturated on 3 nodes. checkpointer pods spiking to ~10Gbps each briefly.
Jamie: confirmed from our side — model-serving latencies jumped for unrelated hosted traffic, looks like egress contention on the top-of-rack.
Alex: interesting — this is the overnight finetune cohort that uses tag=heavy-checkpoint. They hit S3 aggressively then come back and regen KV cache.
ops-bot: incident-alert: Cluster eu-west3: transient tail_latency spike (02:01–02:06 UTC). Auto-mitigation not triggered. Link: https://alerts.company.internal/INC-4492
Dan: quick q — are these jobs on shared pools or on dedicated slices?
Priya: shared pools. We accepted them to save cost, but the snapshot/upload pattern is brutal.
Sara: so two levers: 1) route heavy-checkpoint jobs to a transient dedicated pool (higher $) or 2) apply egress QoS + throttle checkpointing cadence.
Jamie: temporary QoS seems fastest. We can add a per-tenant egress policer for tag=heavy-checkpoint, cap burst to 2Gbps per pod. Low risk and reversible.
Alex: agree. Also need to protect KV cache warmth — maybe bump kvcache TTL for serving models during the window so regen work is limited.
Dan: cost note — spinning a dedicated ephemeral pool for 12h in eu-west3 approx cost: "~monthly-equivalent x day" (will estimate in PR). But it avoids cross-tenant tail impacts.
Priya: quick command I ran on node-12 around the spike:
```
# iftop snapshot
10:01:23 up 3:45,  1 users,  load average: 0.23, 0.10, 0.05
TX: 9.8Gbps  RX: 0.2Gbps
Top talker: pod/finetune-ckpt-7 -> s3.amazonaws.com
```
Alex: thanks. Can we triage with a two-step plan? Short-term QoS + TTL bump; mid-term ephemeral dedicated carveout + scheduler rule to avoid co-locating heavy-checkpoint with low-latency tenants.
Jamie: I can push a QoS rule in the next 20–30m, need PR approval. Will add a label selector for apps with annotation `infra.redwood/egress-class=heavy-checkpoint`.
Dan: I'll draft a cost/benefit for ephemeral pool sizing and run numbers for 12h vs 24h.
Priya: I'll open a quick runbook note and add a guard in the job template to optionally delay checkpoint uploads (staggering).
Sara: long-term: consider scheduler affinity rule that pins KV-cache-sensitive serving slices away from checkpoint-heavy workers. Also maybe pre-warm using a small read-only cache refill window post-checkpoint.
Alex: owners/next steps: Jamie -> QoS PR, Priya -> runbook + job-template guard, Dan -> ephemeral cost estimate + dedicated carveout request, Sara -> scheduler affinity RFC. I'll coordinate and escalate if the QoS doesn't land in 30m.
Jamie: PR link when ready. tagging @env-ops for egress ACL help. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: note: auto-snapshot of QoS rules requires config freeze window; will block if outside maintenance hours.
Alex: good point — we'll request an ad-hoc exception for a short window.
Priya: keeping an eye on the cluster, will report back in 15.
Dan: logging this as follow-up in infra backlog: INFRA-ckpt-egress-2026.
Sara: thanks everyone. If it's helpful I can simulate a worst-case with a 5-node parallel ckpt run on staging to validate TTL bump and QoS behavior.
Alex: do that Sara. We'll circle back after the staging run. :mega:
